bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge code, usbdev_usbif only advanced the frame number and asserted frame_start_o when a real host SOF was received: frame_start_o was tied directly to sof_valid, and the frame register only changed inside the if (sof_valid) branch. There was no fallback when a host SOF was lost or corrupted, so the frame counter froze, no frame-start pulse was generated, and software or isochronous logic waiting for frame boundaries stalled until the next valid SOF arrived. In parallel, usbdev_linkstate detected host loss only with a free-running microsecond counter that directly asserted host_lost after 4.096 ms; it did not produce an intermediate missed-SOF pulse that could be used to synthesize a local frame boundary. The fix also needed to keep the SOF reference pulse host-only, because after introducing locally generated frame-start pulses, driving usb_ref_pulse_o from usb_event_frame would have produced false clock-calibration reference pulses.
bug_info.fix_hint: Add a host-SOF-only sof_valid_o pulse from usb_fs_nb_pe/usbdev_usbif. In usbdev_linkstate, generate sof_missed_o when no valid SOF has been observed for 1005 us, maintain a missed-SOF count for host_lost, and clear the counters on SOF, link inactive, or reset. In usbdev_usbif, use sof_missed_o as do_internal_sof to increment frame_q when no host SOF arrived, and derive frame_start_o from any frame value change. Drive usb_ref_pulse_o in usbdev.sv from usb_event_sof (host-generated only) instead of usb_event_frame, so internally generated SOFs do not create false reference pulses.
